key_insight: inClinico Agent combines machine learning and LLM tools to predict whether clinical trials will meet their primary endpoints across phases I–IV.
clinical_relevance: Trial-level predictions could inform drug-development prioritization, but the abstract does not establish cancer-specific performance or support individual treatment decisions.
method: Models efficacy and safety/toxicity endpoints separately using registration-time features.
Uses target precedent, drug properties, trial design and frozen literature-derived embeddings to reduce outcome leakage.
Combines probability scoring with LLMs, retrieval tools and specialized clinical skills.
evidence_signal: In trials initiated in 2021 or later, AUROC was 0.828 for efficacy (n=2,347) and 0.809 for safety/toxicity (n=1,485); ClinicoBench includes 3,235 ongoing trials for prospective evaluation.
watch_item: Prospective predictive accuracy remains to be established as benchmark trials complete; AUROC alone does not establish probability calibration or decision-making benefit.
paper_title: inClinico Agent for clinical trial endpoint prediction and prospective evaluation
